description: This is a single-panel impact-toughness plot, not a micrograph. The y-axis is "CVN impact energy (J)" (0-250 J, ticks every 50 J) and the x-axis is "Test temperatue (°C)" (printed as such) spanning -200 to 100 °C with ticks every 50 °C. Five labelled curves for two Fe-Mn-Al-C austenitic steels are overlaid on grey reference bands marked "Austenitic stainless", "Duplex", "Ferritic" and "Martensitic". Curves 1 and 2 (solid black lines, open square markers) rise steeply from roughly 65-70 J near -195 °C and plateau at about 150-200 J above -100 °C, crossing the austenitic-stainless band and approaching/crossing each other between about -120 °C and 0 °C. Curve 3 is a red straight line climbing diagonally from near (-190 °C, ~0 J) to about (+20 °C, ~200 J). Curve 4 (filled blue squares joined by a dashed line) starts at ~0 J near -20 °C and reaches only about 60 J at room temperature. Curve 5 (filled red diamonds, with an arrowed label "5") lies at essentially 0 J at about -15 °C and +25 °C. The panel demonstrates that solutionized Fe-Mn-Al-C steels retain high impact energy down to about -100 °C, whereas aging at 550 °C for 16 h (curves 4 and 5) severely embrittles them.

observations.observation: The plot's y-axis is labelled 'CVN impact energy (J)' with a range of 0-250 J and the x-axis is labelled 'Test temperatue (°C)' spanning -200 to 100 °C.

Five numbered curves (1-5) are plotted: curves 1 and 2 use open square markers on solid black lines, curve 3 is a markerless solid red line, curve 4 uses filled blue square markers on a dashed line, and curve 5 uses filled red diamond markers.
Curves 1 and 2 rise from about 65-70 J at roughly -195 °C and plateau at approximately 150-200 J at temperatures above about -100 °C, approaching or crossing one another between -120 °C and 0 °C.
Curve 4 stays below 60 J over its whole range, rising from near zero at about -20 °C to about 60 J at room temperature.
Curve 5 lies at essentially 0 J, with two data points plotted at roughly -15 °C and +25 °C, annotated by an arrow pointing to the label '5'.
Grey shaded background bands labelled 'Austenitic stainless', 'Duplex', 'Ferritic' and 'Martensitic' provide reference toughness ranges against which the five curves are read.
No numeric values are printed at the data points; values can only be read against the axis gridlines.
The caption states curve 1 is Fe-28Mn-5Al-1C solutionized at 1050 °C for 75 min with grain size d = 41 µm.
The caption states curve 2 is Fe-28Mn-5Al-1C solutionized at 1050 °C for 8 h with grain size d = 135 µm.
The caption states curve 3 is Fe-30Mn-10Al-1C-1Si solutionized at 1050 °C for 1 h with grain size d = 120 µm.
The caption states curve 4 is Fe-28Mn-5Al-1C solutionized at 1050 °C for 8 h and aged at 550 °C for 16 h.
The caption states curve 5 is Fe-30Mn-10Al-1C-1Si solutionized at 1050 °C for 1 h and aged at 550 °C for 16 h.

The citing text states the as-solution-treated steels show a high impact energy of 200 J/cm² at room temperature and exhibit a ductile-to-brittle transition at temperatures lower than -100 °C, as indicated by curves 1 to 3.

The citing text states that after aging the CVN impact energy of the Fe-28.3Mn-5.38Al-1.04C steel is much reduced and falls continuously with decreasing test temperature (curve 4), while that of the Fe-30Mn-10Al-1C-1Si alloy is reduced to almost zero (curve 5).
The citing text attributes the simultaneous increase in strength and reduction in impact toughness to the formation of κ-carbide.
